reasons: Aggregation differs: Datadog uses avg by {host}, but the candidate uses sum, which over-counts whenever a host has more than one series of this metric.

Grouping label is unverified: the candidate groups by host_name, but the dataset observes only the label 'state' for nginx.requests and lists no host label, so the PromQL would not group by host as Datadog does.
The Host template variable (prefix host, default *) should become a matcher on the host label (host_name=~"$Host" or the observed equivalent). The candidate drops it entirely.
Quantity and unit are consistent: nginx.requests is a monotonic sum of requests, so rate() gives requests per second, matching nginx.net.request_per_s.
Outcome should not be translated while the aggregation and grouping differ from the source; the request needs a corrected translation or a block.
